regimen_profiles.regimen_role: Locally advanced or metastatic hormone-sensitive prostate cancer
regimen_profiles.clinical_summary: This is androgen deprivation therapy (ADT): it lowers testosterone to help control prostate cancer. With radiotherapy, the aim may be cure; in advanced disease, it is part of ongoing cancer control.
regimen_profiles.treatment_setting: Locally advanced or metastatic hormone-sensitive prostate cancer under NCCP 00478.
regimen_profiles.component_rationale: Goserelin is a GnRH agonist. It first stimulates the pituitary, which may briefly increase testosterone. With continued exposure the pituitary becomes less responsive and testosterone falls. Your team assesses the need for temporary anti-androgen protection against this initial flare.
regimen_profiles.schedule_context: Goserelin 3.6 mg is placed under the skin of the front of the abdomen every 28 days. Your team confirms the exact next date and total treatment duration.
key_points: Goserelin 3.6 mg is placed under the skin of the front of the abdomen every 28 days. Your team confirms the exact next date and total treatment duration.

Regular blood count, kidney and liver tests. Blood glucose and bone blood profile are repeated when clinically indicated. Your team sets the test dates and reviews symptoms, PSA, testosterone when needed and scans.

Tell the team if you take blood-thinning medicines or are very thin. These can increase bleeding risk at implantation. Severe abdominal pain, marked swelling, dizziness or collapse afterwards needs urgent help. Do not stop blood thinners yourself.

treatment_rationale.summary: Androgen deprivation therapy (ADT) lowers testosterone, a hormone that can drive prostate cancer. This medicine is your ADT. Additional cancer tablets, chemotherapy or radiotherapy are separate decisions based on your cancer and overall health. Keep treatment going until your team changes the plan; do not stop because prostate-specific antigen (PSA) has fallen.
treatment_rationale.setting: Locally advanced or metastatic hormone-sensitive prostate cancer under NCCP 00478.
treatment_rationale.line: ADT backbone; select intensification and radiotherapy separately
factors: Disease setting, symptoms, flare risk, cardiovascular risk, interactions, formulation, adherence and patient priorities.
alternatives: Other appropriate ADT modalities including surgical castration; setting-specific combinations and supportive care.
limitations: Hormone suppression is a different endpoint from survival.
Choice depends on disease setting, adherence, interactions, comorbidity and patient priorities; do not rank products using separate trials.

Confirm the exact next injection date. With radiotherapy, ask when hormone treatment starts and ends and how the radiotherapy dates fit. A low PSA does not mean you should stop injections. Tell the team about worsening pain, trouble passing urine or severe headache with vision changes. Rare severe skin reactions: blistering, peeling or sores in the mouth or eyes need urgent medical help. Seek urgent help for a severe headache with vision changes, vomiting, confusion or collapse.

NCCP specifies no renal/hepatic dose modification; the SmPC notes that these populations have not been studied. This is not proof of safety in every organ-failure scenario.
HPRA lists the authorised Eligard 7.5 mg product as not marketed on the checked date. Pharmacy must confirm supply and the exact prescribed product; no automatic strength substitution.

Prior bilateral orchiectomy is a product contraindication. Do not administer an incorrectly prepared dose. Stop further leuprorelin and urgently assess suspected serious skin reactions.

regimen_profiles.clinical_summary: This is androgen deprivation therapy (ADT): it lowers testosterone to help control prostate cancer. With radiotherapy, the aim may be cure; in advanced disease, it is part of ongoing cancer control.
regimen_profiles.treatment_setting: Hormone-dependent advanced prostate cancer, or high-risk localised/locally advanced hormone-dependent disease in combination with radiotherapy.
regimen_profiles.component_rationale: Leuprorelin is a GnRH agonist. Testosterone can rise briefly at the start before continued stimulation switches down the pituitary signal. The depot then maintains suppression between injections. The team assesses flare protection and confirms that testosterone is adequately suppressed.
